name: slide-subtitle-2
text: A browser-based assistant that predicts the material category of a waste photo.

name: overview-problem
text: People often face uncertainty when sorting everyday waste. A wrong choice can contaminate otherwise recyclable material.

name: overview-goal
text: Use a trained image classifier to return a likely waste class and confidence scores through a simple photo or camera workflow.

name: overview-delivers
text:
12-class image classification model
Photo upload and ranked prediction results
Camera preview with capture, review, and predict steps
Mobile-friendly installable web app

Project source: README.md, app.py, templates/index.html.
Presenter cue: Explain that the app is a decision aid. It does not replace local waste instructions.

name: slide-subtitle-3
text: Folder-based image dataset with one directory for each target label.

name: dataset-imbalance
text: 5,325 images, about 34% of the dataset. Class weights help address this imbalance during training.

Project source: models/metadata.json and README.md. Counts sum to 15,515 images.
Presenter cue: Point out the class imbalance and connect it to class-weighted training.

name: slide-subtitle-4
text: The notebook loads labeled folders into a repeatable training and validation pipeline.

name: step-detail-1-92
text: Each class has its own folder. TensorFlow infers labels from folder names.

name: step-detail-2-385
text: 80% training and 20% validation with seed 42 for repeatability.

name: step-detail-3-678
text: Convert images to RGB and resize to 224 x 224 pixels.

name: step-detail-4-971
text: Load in batches of 32 and prefetch the input pipeline.

name: prep-augmentation-copy
text: Random horizontal flip, rotation, zoom, and contrast variation help expose the model to modest changes in object position and image appearance.

Project source: garbage_classification_model.ipynb, sections 3-8.
Presenter cue: Mention that augmentation is used during training, not to alter the user's captured image in the interface.

name: slide-subtitle-5
text: Transfer learning reuses visual features and learns a new classifier for the project classes.

name: model-finetune-copy
text: After training the new head, the notebook unfreezes the final 30 MobileNetV2 layers and fine-tunes them at a lower learning rate.

Project source: garbage_classification_model.ipynb, section 9 and section 11.
Presenter cue: Explain why transfer learning is useful when building a classifier for a focused dataset.

name: slide-subtitle-6
text: The notebook trains a new classification head, then fine-tunes part of the pretrained backbone.

name: training-stage-one-copy
text: Freeze MobileNetV2 and learn the 12-class output layer for up to 12 epochs.

name: training-stage-two-copy
text: Unfreeze the final 30 layers and train for up to 5 more epochs at learning rate 1e-5.

name: training-controls
text:
Class weights address unequal class counts.
Early stopping monitors validation loss and restores best weights.
ReduceLROnPlateau lowers the learning rate when validation loss stalls.
A checkpoint keeps the model with the best validation accuracy.

Project source: garbage_classification_model.ipynb, sections 7, 10, and 11.
Presenter cue: The maximum epochs are upper bounds because early stopping can end training sooner.

name: slide-subtitle-7
text: Saved validation metrics show how the selected model performed on the project validation split.

name: result-caveat
text: Validation split only. The repository does not report an independent test score. New images may differ in lighting, background, or object type.

name: result-abstention
text: Below 40% top score: show an 'Image not confidently classified' popup.

name: limits-list
text:
One image receives one dominant class, even when several objects appear.
The 12 labels do not cover every waste material or local disposal rule.
The saved metadata does not include per-class precision, recall, or a confusion matrix.
Softmax scores are not a calibrated guarantee of correctness.

name: next-list
text:
Add a held-out test set with per-class metrics and error analysis.
Collect more balanced images across phones, lighting, and backgrounds.
Calibrate the 40% low-confidence threshold on a held-out set.
Explore detection for multiple items and verified local disposal guidance.

name: limits-conclusion-text
text: The project demonstrates an end-to-end path from labeled images to a usable waste-classification app.

Project source: models/metadata.json and garbage_classification_model.ipynb. The repository reports validation metrics but no independent test metrics.
